source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 window tutorial, function, expression-syntax, and query-processing documentation; SQLite window documentation; and MySQL 8.4 usage, frame, and restriction documentation. All eight official destinations returned HTTP 200. Default-frame, GROUPS, EXCLUDE, null treatment, and query-placement claims are scoped by dialect and version.

evidence: Checked partition P(r), peer equality, deterministic position, rank, dense rank, frame F(r), and window-aggregate notation.
Checked that partition, analytic order, peer order, deterministic occurrence order, frame, and final presentation order remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Bag occurrences and stable identities are distinguished from equal-looking values.

evidence: Recomputed team A row numbers as 1,2,3,4; ranks as 1,2,2,4; and dense ranks as 1,2,2,3.
Recomputed team A ROWS cumulative sums as 10,30,60,100 and peer-aware cumulative sums as 10,60,60,100.
Recomputed team A lag values as null,10,20,30, partition total 100, and whole-partition last value 40.
Recomputed team B rows, top-two identities, latest identities, and partition count two.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All fixture arithmetic uses exact bounded integers.

evidence: Re-derived rank as one plus strictly earlier occurrence count and dense rank as one plus distinct earlier peer-value count.
Re-derived ROWS frames by ordered position and cumulative peer-aware frames by order value.
Re-derived whole-partition totals and last values from explicit unbounded frame intent.
Re-derived post-window selection as a separate relational layer and showed why earlier filtering changes the population.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No engine-independent claim is made for offset RANGE syntax, default null placement, exclusions, or unsupported features.

evidence: Reviewed empty and singleton partitions, all peers, no peers, duplicate-looking occurrences, and duplicate timestamps with distinct stable IDs.
Reviewed null partition/order/value fields, missing offsets, null addressed values, zero predecessors, reset counters, sparse dates, and exact frame endpoints.
Reviewed one hot partition, incompatible window orders, whole-partition/future-looking frames, memory, spill, concurrency, cancellation, and engine upgrades.
Reviewed tenant filtering, historical corrections, source precedence, snapshots, and multi-statement population changes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Causal use prohibits centered or future-looking frames unless intentional delay is part of the contract.

evidence: Validated one modeled output occurrence per input occurrence and independent computation per team partition.
Validated peer ranks share time values while total (time,id) order determines row position, offsets, and row frames.
Validated partition totals and explicit final values are constant within each partition.
The verifier matched exact four-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The semantic model does not reproduce database types, collation, null placement, execution, or resource behavior.

evidence: Reviewed each A and B occurrence through partition sorting, rank and dense-rank definitions, and predecessor selection.
Reviewed every row-prefix sum and every less-than-or-equal-time peer-aware sum.
Reviewed top-two and latest selection from deterministic positions.
Reviewed whole-partition totals as 10+20+30+40=100 and 5+15=20.
proof_review.notes: No proof of optimizer sort reuse, index satisfaction, bounded memory, or parallel reproducibility is claimed.

evidence: Separated window partition from GROUP BY output, peer order from identity order, analytic order from final order, and frame from partition.
Separated deterministic choice from authoritative choice, missing offset row from null value, and observation count from elapsed time.
Separated logical query boundaries from physical sorts and indexes and portable principles from PostgreSQL, SQLite, and MySQL restrictions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Latest, top, cumulative, moving, deterministic, and efficient claims require the chapter's named assumptions.

evidence: The standard-library finite window semantic model executed successfully through the repository verifier.

Front matter, exact section order, corrected local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
